task: T1: split the image into docker/harness-base.Dockerfile and a thin docker/loop-executor.Dockerfile, and order the two builds in CI. The base carries the LOOP and no model CLI: copy scripts/ and specs/lib/ into HARNESS_HOME=/harness, put $HARNESS_HOME/scripts on PATH, keep the apt set the current file already installs (git, ripgrep, ca-certificates, curl, tini) since those move DOWN into the base rather than being re-solved, and set ENTRYPOINT to run-task.sh under tini exactly as the current file wraps opencode under tini. Do not install opencode, codex or claude in the base — the base having no CLI is the whole point, and it is what lets a third party write FROM harness-base and add their own. The derived image is RENAMED in the same move: docker/loop-executor.Dockerfile and its VERSION become docker/loop-executor-opencode.Dockerfile and docker/loop-executor-opencode.VERSION, because after the split the thing that executes loops is the BASE and the generic name now describes it better than the image carrying one CLI — and loop-executor-codex and loop-executor-claude are the point, so whichever image keeps the bare name reads as the canonical one. Do it now: nothing outside this repo names the image yet, and once the fleet manifests land it is in HARNESS_WORKER_IMAGE, a pull-secret-bearing Job and probably an ImagePolicy. The derived file becomes FROM the base plus the single npm install -g opencode-ai line and nothing else: no apt-get, no second copy of the harness, no re-declared PATH. Add docker/harness-base.VERSION starting at 0.1.0 alongside the existing docker/loop-executor.VERSION. In .github/workflows/build-images.yml the base must be built and PUSHED in a job the derived matrix declares in needs: — a matrix runs its entries in parallel, so a plain third row would race and the derived build would pull a base tag still building; this only bites when both change in the same push, which makes it intermittent and therefore worse to leave implicit, so state the dependency in the workflow graph rather than relying on max-parallel and declaration order. The base is PUBLIC — a private base cannot be extended by anyone else, which defeats the point — so carry the same first-push visibility note the workflow header already has for loop-executor, naming harness-base. Separately fix the tag drift: ghcr.io/mtgibbs/loop-executor:latest has never been pushed by CI and does not exist, yet scripts/exec-container.sh defaults LOOP_IMAGE to it, so point that default at the RENAMED image and a tag CI actually publishes and change docs/loop-container.md's manual fallback to push that same tag — do NOT start publishing :latest, because a mutable tag is exactly what the VERSION-file pattern exists to avoid. Say in a comment in each Dockerfile why the base has no CLI and why the derived file is thin, because the next person to add an executor reads those two files and nothing else. Change no script other than exec-container.sh's default, and no dispatcher code.
